doctrine.summary: HEXSEED tokens describe identity, capability ownership, routing, safety, and surface customization.
doctrine.identity_note: Opalstone may describe the person/identity; Corestone is the CareBloom expression of the INTEGRATE kernel. Mini ARK/Journey is the connective configuration engine and should not resolve as a Corestone alias.
doctrine.naming_identity_policy: Mini ARK is the active implementation name. Journey is the emerging product/system identity and must not become a parallel codebase or casual rename before an approved migration.
doctrine.empty_folder_policy: Never delete a folder solely because it is empty.
doctrine.routing_policy: Files live in their natural canonical home first; specificity is added through representations such as shortcuts, manifests, tags, and project views.
doctrine.token_reception_policy: Everything that enters Mini ARK either carries an existing token or receives a provisional token at reception. Source document names and filenames are primary token evidence because they often encode operator intent. Routing and placement follow token identity.
doctrine.ambient_congruence_policy: Corestone/HEXSEED should continuously pursue user-computer congruence by the least resistant, least disturbing path available. Always observe; auto-apply only safe, reversible, high-confidence, low-cost maintenance; throttle during active foreground or heavy compute; record receipts and preserve rollback for autonomous changes; ask only for ambiguity, judgment, destructive action, unclear ownership, or expensive/disruptive work.
doctrine.resource_doctrine: Corestone is always aware, not always busy. Foreground responsiveness wins; heavy compute makes stewardship throttle or sleep; idle and low-load periods allow deeper maintenance.
doctrine.mutation_policy: Detect and propose first; execute only through approved, reversible operations.
doctrine.prompt_policy: Do not create routine 'run organizer' prompts or buttons for housekeeping. Prompts are for real judgment, not ordinary maintenance.
auto_apply_policy: broken-reference repair where destination is unambiguous
do_not_auto_apply_policy: changes with unclear ownership or destination
doctrine.visual_identity_policy: HEXSEED_v4.ico is the selected canonical HEXSEED identity icon. Expression profiles may provide profile-specific icons, but the foundation icon remains the stable HEXSEED mark unless explicitly changed.

visual_identity.selection_note: Chosen for practical icon readability and stable HEXSEED identity: outer hex, central seed/crystal, and clear silhouette at small sizes.
visual_identity.mini_ark_journey_icon_policy: Use mini_ark.ico for the active C:\mini_ark implementation. Hold journey.ico for the future Journey identity and do not apply it until the deliberate Journey migration is approved.
visual_identity.selected_carebloomos_app_icon_note: Selected as the one CareBloomOS application icon. The bloom-within-bloom mark has the strongest standalone silhouette, says CareBloom without requiring a secondary glyph, communicates the recursive multi-domain system, and avoids over-specifying what the OS is currently doing. The PNG is the source art; the ICO is the Windows/application icon artifact.

carebloomos_icon_audition.nursery_policy: Hold the other candidates briefly for genuine reuse opportunities. Do not build a permanent hierarchy around them; prune them if no real use appears.

visual_identity.carebloom_identity_policy: Use cAREBLOOM_BABY.png as the selected CareBloomOS application icon. The other CareBloomOS icon candidates remain nursery assets only, not a canonical semantic hierarchy.
visual_identity.stone_icon_policy: Folders or surfaces explicitly named for a CareBloom stone may use that stone's canonical icon. Filesystem application must be previewed first and should write only presentation metadata such as desktop.ini unless explicitly approved.

representations.surface: CareBloomOS project views may reference assets without becoming the source of truth
